description: This course introduces Human-Centred Computing as a foundational approach to designing computing systems that fit human needs, abilities, and values. Students learn to frame problems from a user perspective, understand users and contexts through empirical methods, and iteratively design, prototype, and evaluate interactive systems. The course emphasizes evidence-based design, usability and user experience evaluation, accessibility and inclusive design, and ethical considerations in real-world deployment. Through hands-on exercises and a team project, students develop skills in human-centred design and learn to communicate design decisions clearly, preparing them to build usable, responsible, and impactful computing systems across domains.
